prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1449; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports vehicles made contact at low speed in a lane near an intersection. Insured vehicle sustained front bumper and hood damage. Claimant driver reported neck pain and stiffness at the scene and was transported to urgent care. Liability appears disputed pending statements. Vehicle inspection assigned.

Entry 2: Claimant is now represented by counsel. Letter of representation received and logged. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and treatment records. Reserve set for bodily injury and property damage pending review.

Entry 3: Field appraiser completed inspection of both vehicles. Damage consistent with low-speed impact. Airbag did not deploy in either vehicle. Repair estimate received from body shop and reviewed. Rental coverage confirmed for insured while repairs are underway. Photos uploaded to file.

Entry 4: Received initial medical records from claimant's provider. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with whiplash-type symptoms. Treatment plan includes physical therapy and follow-up in several weeks. Attorney's office has submitted a demand package indicating ongoing treatment. Records under review by claims team and nurse reviewer assigned.

Entry 5: Liability analysis ongoing. Statements from both drivers differ on signal phase and lane position. Independent witness contacted, callback requested. Recommended a structured settlement discussion with counsel once medical review is complete. File remains open with diary set for follow-up.
